425	### D.4 Weld transfer
426	
427	The weld transfer formula (`body_transfer`, weld case, BM3) is defined as:
428	
429	`for each actor a with body_id == absorbed:  pos_curr' = pos_curr + frame_shift_px;  body_id' = surviving_body_id;  pos_prev' = pos_curr';  sub' = sub;  last_octant' = last_octant;   host-body actors unchanged;   the absorbed pose row is deleted`
430	
431	**Variables:**
432	
433	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
434	|---|---|---|---|---|
435	| `frame_shift_px` | int pair | on Layout's 24-px grid (`LY D.6`), may be negative | Layout's `attach_section` return record (LY-16): `offset_b - offset_b_old` | the absorbed body's frame origin expressed in the host's frame; every absorbed section gains it |
436	| `pos_curr` | int pair | absorbed body frame | `body.state` | the actor's foot origin before the weld |
437	| `surviving_body_id`, `absorbed_body_id` | int | live Layout ids, distinct | Layout return record | the host keeps its id (the home-ship socket is passed first, LY-16) |
438	| `n_moved` | int | 0 to `MAX_ACTORS` | calculated | actors on the absorbed body |
439	
440	**Output Range:** host-frame coordinates; `sub` and `last_octant` untouched because a whole-pixel shift cannot disturb a residue. **Preservation property P-W:** for every moved actor `actor_section` and `actor_local_px` (D.10) are identical before and after, because the absorbed sections' offsets gain exactly `frame_shift_px` and so do the positions. Dirty keys: one `ACT` per moved actor plus one `BODY` for the deleted pose row (D.13). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The event payload's `frame_delta_px` is `+frame_shift_px` (3.7), the value the Pipeline rebases by.
441	
442	**Example (`LY D.6` airlock, `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`):** an actor on the derelict body at `(100, 50)` in section 3 (pre-weld offset `(0, 0)`) becomes `(676, 146)` on the home-ship body; `actor_local_px` before `(100, 50) - (0, 0) = (100, 50)`, after `(676, 146) - (576, 96) = (100, 50)`. A host actor at `(300, 100)` is untouched and raises no `BODY_TRANSFER`. If the absorbed body had been welded before (`offset_b_old != (0, 0)`), `frame_shift_px` is the difference, not the new offset.
443	
444	### D.5 Detach transfer
445	
446	The detach transfer formula (`body_transfer`, detach case, BM4) is defined as:
447	
448	`offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s) + frame_shift_px  if s in moved_sections[]  else  section_offset(s);   side(a) = NEW  iff  pos_curr(a) in cells(s) + offset_pre(s)  for some s in moved_sections[];   NEW actors:  pos_curr' = pos_curr - frame_shift_px,  body_id' = new_body_id,  pos_prev' = pos_curr',  sub' = (0, 0),  last_octant' = last_octant;   KEEP actors unchanged;   world_new = world_old + frame_shift_px,  vel_new = vel_old + drift`
449	
450	BM4 runs AFTER Layout's `detach_section` (Assembly's call order; LY-16, LY-17), so Layout has already re-based the moved sections; Body recovers the pre-cut geometry by adding `frame_shift_px` back for `moved_sections[]` only (the call-order trap, BDY-23). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* BM4 first evaluates the cap guard: an actor on the old body whose box overlaps `cap_rects[]` makes it return `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` with nothing written (BDY-24 (iii)). The foot ORIGIN picks the side; a box straddling the seam is not split.
451	
452	**Variables:**
453	
454	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
455	|---|---|---|---|---|
456	| `moved_sections[]` | list of section ids | non-empty | Layout's `detach_section` return record (LY-17) | the sections now in `C_new` |
457	| `frame_shift_px` | int pair | on the 24-px grid | the same record; `offset_old(m)` for `m = min(section_id)` over `C_new` (`LY D.12`) | the new frame origin expressed in the old frame; moved sections LOSE it |
458	| `cells(s)` | half-open cell set, section-local | the section's rooms and the rectangles it owns, incl. its own 24-px hull footprint and hatch rectangles | Layout template | containment is by floor area, never by bounding box |
459	| `pos_curr(a)` | int pair | old body frame | `body.state` | the foot origin on the detach tick |
460	| `world_old`, `vel_old` | int pair | D.7 ranges | `body.state` pose row | the old body's pose |
461	| `drift` | int pair | magnitude `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK` (default 0, exterior only) | Body-owned | added to `vel_new` along the separation axis, away from the old body (BDY-28) |
462	
463	**Output Range:** new-body coordinates for NEW actors; KEEP actors untouched. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The event payload's `frame_delta_px` is `-frame_shift_px` (3.7), the value the Pipeline rebases by. **Preservation property P-D:** moved actors keep `(actor_section, actor_local_px)` exactly. **Conservation:** with `abs(a) = world(body_of(a)) + pos_curr(a)`, detach conserves `abs` exactly for every actor on both sides (at default drift 0, and drift touches `vel` only). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Range guard.** The formula's `world_new = world_old + frame_shift_px` and `vel_new = vel_old + drift` must stay inside the D.7 ranges or the next autosave is rejected (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`): `can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` answers `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` / `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` before the cut, and an `apply` that was not guarded applies BDY-23's two-case net and returns `OK` (world overflow: `world` saturated per axis and `vel` set to `(0, 0)`; velocity overflow: `vel` saturated per axis; counted `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` where applicable and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`), waiving the `abs` conservation of the exterior pose on that defect branch only. **Example:** `world_old = (4,194,304, 0)` and `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)` gives `world_new.x = 4,194,880`, out of range: validate rejects the cut; an unguarded apply stores `(4,194,304, 96)` with `vel (0, 0)`, and `restore(snapshot())` accepts it. An origin lying in no section (an exterior gap, a defect) stays on `C_keep` and counts `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`. A weld followed by a cut of the same seam is not in general an identity on `pos_curr` (BDY-23), so round-trip criteria assert `abs` and the section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`.
464	
465	**Example (`LY D.12` chain: sections 1 `(0, 0)`, 3 `(576, 96)`, 4 `(1056, 96)` on body 1, cut at seam (1, 3)):** `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`, new offsets 3 `(0, 0)`, 4 `(480, 0)`. Reconstruction: `offset_pre(3) = (0, 0) + (576, 96) = (576, 96)`, `offset_pre(4) = (480, 0) + (576, 96) = (1056, 96)`, `offset_pre(1) = (0, 0)`. An actor at old-body `(600, 200)` (section-3 local `(24, 104)`, assuming that cell lies in a section-3 room: the fixture fixes offsets, not extents) moves to `(24, 104)`; an actor in section 4 at `(1100, 150)` moves to `(524, 54)` (local `(44, 54)` before and after); an actor in section 1 at `(300, 100)` stays. An actor with origin `(690, 282)` lies in section 1's east wall footprint `[672, 696)` and its box reaches column 697 into section 3's footprint `[696, 720)`: the seam's hatch rectangles overlap it, so BM4 called with `cap_rects[]` = those two plates returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` and writes nothing (BDY-24 (iii)); the side rule alone (BM4 with `cap_rects[]` empty, the unit-test surface) would keep it on `C_keep` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)*. With `world_old = (1000, 500)` the new pose row is `(1576, 596)`; the section-3 actor's `abs` is `(1000, 500) + (600, 200) = (1600, 700)` before and `(1576, 596) + (24, 104) = (1600, 700)` after.
466	
467	### D.6 Pod transfer
468	
469	The pod transfer formula (`body_transfer`, pod case, BM5; Web Map & Transit is Designed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional — undesigned")*) is defined as:
470	
471	`pos_curr' = to_pos;  body_id' = to_body_id;  pos_prev' = pos_curr';  sub' = (0, 0);  last_octant' = last_octant;  carry_ref untouched (the Controller's)`
472	
473	**Variables:**

486	The world pose integration formula is defined as:

488	`for b in ascending body_id (rows present):  if  abs(world_x + vel_x) <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT  and  abs(world_y + vel_y) <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT  then  world' = world + vel  else  vel' = (0, 0), world' = world, BDY_WORLD_LIMIT += 1;     canvas_offset(b) = world(b) - world(avatar_body)`

490	One add per tick, before any actor steps (BDY-9). With the reset `off_prev = off_curr = (912, 240)` and the offset steps once; without it `off_prev` would still be `(900, 240)` and the hull would slide 12 px across the following frame, a smear across a discontinuity the exterior layer was never meant to animate. 506	
507	The docking invariant formula is defined as:
508	
509	`docked(a, b, frame_shift_px) = ( vel(a) == vel(b) )  and  ( world(b) - world(a) == frame_shift_px );     delta_abs = frame_shift_px - ( world(b) - world(a) )`   (`a` = host, `b` = absorbed)
510	
511	`delta_abs` is the change in an absorbed actor's `abs` position at the weld (`abs_after - abs_before`) and equally the jump the absorbed hull makes in the exterior layer; its sign is defined once, here: **new minus old**. The cited budgets, restated against the right denominators: eight actors (`MAX_ACTORS`) at the cited 0.05 ms are 0.4 ms, 20 % of the kernel's 2 ms P3 target; four actors at the cited 0.2 ms are 10 %. `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is only a logging threshold and is not the denominator.
623	
624	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What the model above leaves out, and the whole-hook budget.** The figures above price only the moving-actor path, with the literal stepper, and the `c_r` 0.25 us of the earlier example was an **unmeasured illustration** (struck in the example above) (every constant is **[UNV]** until spike S1; it is not a design figure and no criterion gates on it). The full model, with the analytic clamp as the baseline (BDY-15) and the stepper only as the test oracle:
625	
626	`T_move = c_q + K * c_r * 3 + c_commit`   (ordinary moving actor, clamp against each returned rectangle's near edge, about `3 * K` tests)
627	`T_exempt = c_q + K * c_r + n_sub * (|E| * c_ov + c_sec) + c_commit`   (exempt actor, `n_sub <= abs(step_x) + abs(step_y) <= 6` candidate sub-steps, `c_ov` one per-rectangle overlap area, `c_sec` one `section_at` call for the exit-containment test, BDY-29)
628	`T_idle = c_commit`   (stationary: residue update and commit, no query)
629	`T_hook = n_bodies_moving * c_pose + sum over actors of (T_move | T_exempt | T_idle) + c_diag`
630	
631	Worst-case fixtures, committed with the criterion (AC-BDY-68): (W1) 8 actors all moving against the K = 16 cluster; (W2) 8 actors all EXEMPT at the abutting-pair cap with `|E| = 2`, all pressing east so every tick evaluates `E` and calls `section_at` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: W2 is NOT the most expensive exempt case; east is refused at the first candidate sub-step there, so `n_sub` = 1 and each actor pays one `|E| * c_ov + c_sec`)*; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (W2b) 8 actors all EXEMPT inside F7's single 24 x 96 rectangle (a box wholly inside one rectangle, `|E| = 1`, the section-set stub answering a section for every candidate origin), octant 1 at `v_eff` 3, so every candidate sub-step is admitted and `n_sub` reaches its bound of 6: `T_exempt = c_q + K * c_r + 6 * (c_ov + c_sec) + c_commit` per actor, the most expensive exempt tick; (W2c) the mixed fixture, 4 moving actors (W1's K = 16 cluster), 2 exempt actors (W2b) and 2 idle actors, the realistic bound on a busy tick; (W3) 8 bodies all with `vel != 0` and 8 idle actors (pose step plus 8 commits); (W4) Suit's reads, 8 seats each calling `actor_section` and `actor_local_px` once per tick for `suit.vitals` (BDY-29: 8 `section_at` calls per tick from the consumer and none from the hook itself), added to the hook total of W1 and of W2b; (W5) a weld or cut tick, the detection event of BDY-16 for every actor on the touched bodies with the trapped-actor probe for each actor whose start box has `E` non-empty: `T_event = n_touched * c_q + n_flagged * 192 * (|E| * c_ov + c_sec)` (192 = 4 directions x `TILE_PX` 48), at most 8 x 192 = 1,536 overlap tests and 1,536 `section_at` calls, once per event and never per tick. **Separate bounds for moving and exempt actors *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*:** a moving actor costs at most `3 * K` box-versus-rectangle tests; an exempt actor costs at most `K` rectangle tests plus `n_sub * |E|` overlap evaluations plus `n_sub` `section_at` calls (`n_sub <= 6`), a different shape that `3 * K` does not describe (AC-BDY-117 gates each on its own count). **Catch-up worst frame:** a late frame runs `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4 ticks (BDY-32), so the worst frame cost is `4 * T_hook` of the more expensive of W2b and W2c, plus W4; on the cited per-actor figure the arithmetic for 8 actors is `4 * 0.4 ms = 1.6 ms`, 27 % of `FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS` 6.0 (the budget of a frame that runs `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks; a one-tick frame is 4.0), an upper bound on the cited figure only, to be replaced by the S1 measurement *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was stated as 40 % of `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, the wrong denominator)*. **Spike S1 is a hard prerequisite** of closing the Body hook story *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: every wall-clock figure in this section is gated on the two reference machines of delegated ruling R12 and is *pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK*. **RM-DESKTOP** is the minimum-spec desktop: Windows 10/11 64-bit; a 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; a GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; Until S1 has recorded a number on both machines no figure in this section is a gate; the S1 baseline then becomes the +25 % reference (AC-BDY-117 (b)). The `STEP_BUDGET_MS` check is the logged share of the whole hook, not of one actor.
632	
633	### D.13 Dirty-key encoding
634	
635	The dirty-key encoding formula is defined as:
636	
637	`key = (KIND << 32) | id;     KIND: BODY = 2 (the shared family), ACT = 4`
638	
639	Layout's encoding (registry `layout_dirty_key_encoding`; Layout's KINDs are SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3), keys being namespaced by block, so reusing `BODY` 2 inside `body.state` is legal and `ACT` 4 is unused by Layout. Every mutator and the hook mark explicitly (4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the setter, **verified-from-docs**, `breaking-changes.md` 4.6 to 4.7).
640	
641	**Variables:**
642	
643	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
644	|---|---|---|---|---|
645	| `KIND` | int | 2 or 4 | Layout's encoding; Body adds `ACT` | key family |
646	| `id` | int | `body_id` or `actor_id`, below 2^32 | Layout / the block counter `next_actor_id` | the entity |
647	| `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` | int | 256 | registry (kernel) | per block per tick, above which the kernel reports `ALL` |
648	
649	**Output Range:** a unique 64-bit key per `(KIND, id)`. Counts: the hook marks one `ACT` per actor that moved or whose `sub` changed (at most `MAX_ACTORS`) plus one `BODY` per body with `vel != (0, 0)` (at most `MAX_BODIES`); BM3 marks `n_moved` `ACT` plus 1 `BODY`; BM4 the same; BM1, BM2, BM5, BM6, BM7 mark 1 to 2. The worst-tick union is at most 16 distinct keys at the defaults (8 actors, `MAX_BODIES` 8) and *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "32 at the tops of both ranges (16 actors, 16 bodies)" counted 16 bodies, but `MAX_BODIES` is Layout's allocation cap of 8, and the key count cannot exceed the number of bodies that can exist)* **24 at the top of the `MAX_ACTORS` range (16 actors + `MAX_BODIES` 8 bodies)**, 10 to 16 times under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, so overflow cannot happen. A body with non-zero `vel` marks its `BODY` key every tick because its `world` changes, which keeps the delta stream non-empty for the whole pod leg; VS-B replication should send `world` only on a `vel` change (ADR-BODY-02).
650	
651	**Example:** `ACT/3 = (4 << 32) | 3 = 17,179,869,187`; `BODY/1 = (2 << 32) | 1 = 8,589,934,593`. A weld with 8 absorbed actors marks 8 `ACT` + 1 `BODY` = 9 keys.
652	
653	### D.14 Move-octant reset
654	
655	The move-octant reset formula is defined as:
656	
657	`move_octant = NONE if v_eff == 0;  else octant if octant in 0..7;  else last_octant if (STOP_DECEL_TICKS > 0 and last_octant != NONE)  (decel-ladder sub-case, dormant at STOP_DECEL_TICKS 0);  else NONE, counting BDY_OCTANT_INVALID;     reset  iff  move_octant != last_octant;     on reset  sub := (0, 0)  BEFORE the step;     after the step  last_octant := move_octant`
658	
659	The predicate compares the move octant with Body's OWN persisted `last_octant` (0 to 7, 8 = NONE), never with the Controller's restore-normalised `octant := NONE` (PC-17), which is what makes a restore with the key still held continue the residue (BDY-31). The decel-ladder sub-case (octant NONE with `v_eff > 0`, PCI D.5) is **provisional**: it exists so the ladder is not silently broken if `STOP_DECEL_TICKS` is ever raised above its MVP default 0, where it is never taken (CP-8). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The branch is gated** on `STOP_DECEL_TICKS > 0 and last_octant != NONE`: at the shipping default 0 an octant NONE or invalid with `v_eff > 0` (garbage input, a corrupt restore) yields NONE, so the actor is IDLE, `moved (0, 0)`, `sub` reset, `last_octant := NONE`, `BDY_OCTANT_INVALID` +1, and it never keeps walking its stale heading; and `last_octant` is read as an octant only when it is 0..7, so `UNIT[8]` is never indexed.
660	
661	**Variables:**
662	
663	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
664	|---|---|---|---|---|
665	| `octant` | int | 0 to 7 or NONE (8) | `controller.state` (written by `controller.step`) | the committed movement direction; any value outside 0 to 8 is treated as NONE (`BDY_OCTANT_INVALID`) |
666	| `v_eff` | int | 0 to 3 | `controller.state` `gait_effective` (PCI D.4) | zero for a stop, STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD, `IN_POD`, CHANNELLING and the end of a ladder |
667	| `last_octant` | int | 0 to 8 | `body.state` `actors[].last_octant` (persisted) | the octant the last step integrated; a different field from `controller.state`'s ladder memory of the same name (BDY-7) |
668	| `sub` | int pair | -255 to 255 | `body.state` | the residue of D.1 |
669	
670	**Output Range:** boolean `reset`. `sub` resets on a stop, on any `v_eff == 0` tick and on any octant change; it does NOT reset on a gait change in one octant (walk to run keeps the residue), on a refused step, or in `post_restore`. A reset at `last_octant == NONE` is a no-op (the persisted invariant is `sub == (0, 0)` whenever `last_octant == NONE`, BDY-31).
671	
672	**Example (re-fixtured PC-18 test 10):** NE (octant 1) at `v_eff` 2; after tick 2 `sub.x = 212`, `last_octant = 1`. Snapshot, restore, hold the same key (the Adapter's resync lands in P2 of the first post-restore tick, BDY-31): tick 3 reads `move_octant = 1 == 1`, no reset, `sub.x = 212 + 362 = 574`, `step = 2`, `sub.x = 62`, the uninterrupted cadence (1, 1, 2). Had the residue been zeroed, tick 3 would read `step = 1`, `sub.x = 106`, a different pixel path from tick 3 on. Key released across the save/load window: `v_eff = 0`, `move_octant = NONE != 1`, reset, identical to a stop. Octant change NE (1) to E (0) with `sub = (106, -106)`: `move_octant 0 != last_octant 1`, so `sub` resets to `(0, 0)` before the first E step, which moves exactly 2 px (the PCI D.4 fixture). Walk to run in octant 1: `move_octant == last_octant`, no reset. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Garbage input, ladder off (`STOP_DECEL_TICKS` 0):** `octant` 9, `v_eff` 2, `last_octant` 1: octant 9 is invalid so the move octant is NONE (the gated branch is not taken), `NONE != 1` resets `sub` to `(0, 0)`, `last_octant := 8`, the actor is IDLE and does not move, `BDY_OCTANT_INVALID` +1. `octant` NONE, `v_eff` 2, `last_octant` 8: the move octant is NONE, equal to `last_octant`, so the reset is a no-op, the actor is IDLE, no `UNIT` lookup is made and `BDY_OCTANT_INVALID` +1.

119	### Core Rules
120	
121	Rule ids are `BDY-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section); acceptance criteria are `AC-BDY-n`; BM1 to BM7 are Body's mutators; `can_*` are its pure precondition reads. Locked constants and formulas from the kernel, the Graph, the Controller, the Pipeline and Layout are used by name with their registry values and are never restated differently (a needed different value would be a CONFLICT line in Open Questions, never a new number): `TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 (owner: the art bible), `V_WALK` 2, `V_RUN` 3, `V_CARRY` 1 base px per tick, the 1/256 fixed point with its `UNIT` table (256 cardinal, 181 diagonal), `MAX_BODIES` 8, `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` 2,000, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, `JOLT_PX` 0. Body-new constants (`FOOT_BOX_W`, `FOOT_BOX_H`, `MAX_ACTORS`, `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`, `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK`, `SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS`) are listed in Tuning Knobs and registered after this GDD is final (Cross-References); any not fixed by a ruling is tagged `[PLACEHOLDER]` (`SWEEP_COST_LOG_MS` is `[PLACEHOLDER]`, suggested 0.05 ms, the per-actor figure of PCI:1078, a logging threshold only). Contracts with undesigned or in-flight systems are marked **(provisional — <system> undesigned)** and name what that GDD must repeat. Conflicts, clarifications and asks are marked **CONFLICT**, **CLARIFY** and **ASK** and are routed in Cross-References and Open Questions, never silently resolved in a neighbour's text. Each rule closes with *Decides:* (the pillar, ruling or sibling rule it serves) and a test tag: (auto) automated, (lint) static check, (review) design review, (spike) engine spike.
122	
123	#### 1.1 Identity, ownership and the no-physics-server rule
124	
125	**BDY-1 — One body per welded set; Body adds pose, not geometry.** A body's identity is Layout's `body_id` (LY-18: Layout allocates it from `next_body_id`, first id 1, and owns `bodies[]`, `section_instances[].body_id`, offsets and `welds[]`). Body stores, per `body_id`, only the frame's POSE (`world_x`, `world_y`), its velocity (`vel_x`, `vel_y`) and the reserved `heading_q`, and, per actor, the actor's body-frame state. Body never allocates, retires or edits a `body_id`, section membership, offset, rectangle, socket, seam or hatch state. The composite welded ship is therefore ONE body in exactly the sense the index means: one frame, one pose row, one rectangle set (`solid_in(body_id, aabb)`), however many sections are welded into it. *Decides:* LY-18, LY-35; P1. (review) grep this GDD for `next_body_id`, `welds[]` and `offset_px` as Body-written fields: zero hits.
126	
127	**BDY-2 — The interior is a pose-invariant integer frame.** Every simulation fact about the interior — a foot box, a `solid_in` rectangle, `pos_curr`, an Emitter anchor, Suit's room lookup, the interior camera pose — is a body-frame integer. **Nothing keyed on a body-frame coordinate reads `world_*` or `vel_*`.** A body that moves in the exterior moves nothing inside it, so the moving-platform problem does not exist as an engine problem; a body in motion and a body at rest produce a byte-identical interior (D.9 states the invariance; the acceptance fixture sets a non-zero `vel` on the avatar's body, runs 600 ticks and compares `canonical_encode(payload["actors"])` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*). Rotation is never a simulation fact (BDY-26). *Decides:* R1, R6, P1, PIPE C2 (PIPE:153). (lint + auto)
128	
129	**BDY-3 — No Godot physics server on any simulation path.** `RigidBody2D`, `CharacterBody2D`, `StaticBody2D`, `AnimatableBody2D`, `PhysicsBody2D`, `Area2D`, `PhysicsServer2D`, `move_and_slide`, `move_and_collide`, `test_move`, `body_test_motion`, engine tile collision and navigation meshes appear in this GDD only in rejected-alternative text and in the lint criterion, which extends the Controller's lint (PCI:900) from the controller, body and presenter directories to the whole Body module and to Layout's (zero matches for that token set; zero matches in the block and the hook for `randi`, `randf`, `randomize`, `Time.`, `OS.get_ticks`, `Engine.get_physics_frames`, float-typed declarations and non-integer `Vector2(`; the PROJECTOR script is the only Body script allowed to name `Node2D`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The token grep is not sufficient on its own, because GDScript type inference can silently produce a float** (`var x := a / b` on ints is integer division, but `var y := a * 0.5` or an untyped `Variant` path is a float that no token list names). The lint therefore also **promotes the GDScript typing warnings to errors for every script under the Body and Layout directories** — `UNTYPED_DECLARATION`, `INFERRED_DECLARATION`, `UNSAFE_*`, `NARROWING_CONVERSION`, `INTEGER_DIVISION`, `INFERENCE_ON_VARIANT` — and CI fails on any warning raised by a file in those directories (the project-setting scope is global or per-script in Godot, **[UNV]** whether a directory scope exists; the CI step filters the warning output by path in either case). `INTEGER_DIVISION` makes every `/` on integers an error unless annotated, which leaves exactly ONE annotated `/` site, inside `trunc_div` (`floor_div` calls it, BDY-35). The 2D server that exists is Godot Physics 2D (**verified-from-docs**: `modules/physics.md`, "2D physics UNCHANGED (still Godot Physics 2D)"; Jolt is the 3D default since 4.6 and does not apply to 2D). Body relies on it for nothing; the one candidate use is presentation-only debris at Vertical Slice, excluded from `ALL_SIM` (ADR-BODY-05). *Rejected alternatives:* one `RigidBody2D` or `CharacterBody2D` per ship with engine collision shapes built from Layout (contradicts four designed GDDs, makes G3 depend on a recorded physics replay, adds an unmeasured shape rebuild per weld and per cut, and lets rotation leak inside, PIPE C2); an engine-physics exterior hybrid (a second authority for pose). *Decides:* R1, R13, KRN:123 (G3), Guard rail 3. (lint) → ADR-BODY-01, ADR-BODY-05.
130	
131	**BDY-4 — Who is an actor; what is not.** An `actors` row has `kind SEAT | AGENT`. MVP rows are `SEAT` only: one per bound player seat. **A horror holds its own position**: of the two paths (keep a position in its own state block and call the pure `LocomotionStep` of BDY-10, or register `AGENT` rows here), Horror Entities chose path 1 (HE-23: position, residue and `last_octant` in `horror.state`, movement only through `LocomotionStep` with Body's foot box; consistency pass 2026-10-27), so MVP `AGENT` rows stay unused, and a horror's footprint is a Graph trail, never a Body fact. **No prop is an actor**: loose items are Interaction records in section-local pixels (IA-28, LY-22: "a weld or a detach moves nothing"); static props and machinery are Layout rectangles; a thrown glowstick lands analytically (IA-29). A Vertical Slice movable prop adds one `kind` here and one bump-list entry in Layout (LY:229) deliberately. **Orphaned bodies persist**: a body left with no actor keeps its pose row; membership and discard are Layout's, Assembly's and Web Map's (`discard_section_geometry`); Body offers `actors_on(body_id)` and `body_count()` for their decisions. Filter-only phantoms (hallucination class (a)) have no Body row. *Decides:* R9, R18, R19; P4. (review)
132	
133	#### 1.2 The block
134	
135	**BDY-5 — `body.state` is one SHARED `SIM` block.** Registration (CR-8, with `supported_versions` from SL-15 item 2, SL:224): `block_id body.state`; owner Ship Body; `class SIM`; `persist true`; `persist_scope WORLD`; `scope SHARED`; `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`; `schema_version 1`; `supported_versions [1]`; `restore_after: [layout.state]`; exactly one hook, `body.integrate`; exactly one `PROJECTOR` subscriber, `body.projector`. Two sparse tables: `bodies` keyed by `body_id` (Layout's id) and `actors` keyed by `actor_id`, plus the block-local counter `next_actor_id` (CR-8: entity ids are allocated by the owning block from a counter stored inside it). Body repeats what Layout asked it to repeat (LY-18): it owns `body.state` (pose, velocity, actor positions); its `restore_after` is `[layout.state]`; and it owns the physics `PROJECTOR` slot (BDY-33). *Rejected:* `PER_PLAYER` scope (bodies and pods have no PlayerId); two blocks (`body.state` and `body.frames`) — a second restore node and a second owner registration where EM-1 names one. *Decides:* R2, EM-1, SL:288; CR-8. (auto: registration lint) → ADR-BODY-02.

**CR-8. State-block registry contract.** An owner registers: `block_id` (unique, namespaced, e.g. `graph.state`); `owner`; `schema_version` (bumped on any serialized-shape change); `class` ∈ {`SIM`, `PERCEPTION_OUT`} (CR-12); `persist` (false = derived, rebuilt after load) and, when true, `persist_scope` ∈ {`WORLD`, `PROFILE`} — `WORLD` blocks live in the world snapshot and roll back on `request_restore`; `PROFILE` blocks (decoded rules, lore, scars: Pillar 5's "never knowledge") live outside it and are never rolled back by a world restore; `scope` ∈ {`SHARED`, `PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId}; `gameplay` (bool, mandatory: true when a gameplay verb can change the block; false only for settings, menu and save-request state — the CR-16 paused-write test) and `interpolated` (bool, default false: when true the kernel calls the owner's `commit_baseline()` at P4 so the previous/current pair rolls exactly once per tick, and after a restore or an owner-declared teleport/reset the owner calls `snap_baseline(key)` so presentation never interpolates across a discontinuity) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `repl_hint` ∈ {`HOST_ONLY`, `SHARED_SUMMARY`, `OWNER_PRIVATE`} — mandatory now though unused until VS-B, so no block ever ships without the decision; `snapshot(ctx)` (delivers its plain data through `ctx.put(payload)` and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; canonical state only, deterministic ordering, entity references by stable ID, no derived caches; **the payload is a deep copy** — `duplicate_deep()` for Dictionary/Array, `duplicate()` for Packed arrays, which GDScript passes by reference — never a reference into live state); `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` (whole-block replace; **copies in** and never retains a reference to `data`, so two restores from one payload cannot alias; the owner migrates from `stored_version`; an unsupported version is a reported failure through the fault channel, never a silent default) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `default_state(ctx)` (when a save lacks the block; `ctx.put(state)`); `post_restore(ctx)` (after *all* blocks restore: resolve cross-block IDs, rebuild caches, check invariants); `read_view(ctx)` (the kernel's view-issuing surface calls it and hands the reader `ctx.put(view)`'s content: a getter-only facade or a copy — never a live container, CR-12); `commit_baseline(ctx)` and `snap_baseline(key, ctx)` for `interpolated` blocks; optionally `init_world(world_seed, ctx)` (a new-game step, CR-18); optionally `binding_source(ctx)` (delivers `[(player_id, entity_id)]` ascending through `ctx.put`; content.content: **BDY-16 — Overlap exemption: the body is never displaced, and an exempt actor can only leave.** Let `E` be the set of SOLID rectangles the actor's foot box intersects **at the start of the actor's tick** (fixed for that tick). Members of `E` arise from a door leaf that closed under the actor, a restore of an older save against a changed template, or a template defect *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* (a cut can no longer cap a hatch under an actor: BM4 refuses it, BDY-24 (iii)). For an actor with a non-empty `E`, a 1-px sub-step on either axis is admitted iff **for every `r` in `E`, `|box_after ∩ r| <= |box_before ∩ r|`** (overlap measured in cells; D.11 states `ov(r)`) **and the destination foot origin lies in a section of the actor's body (exit containment, below)**; every rectangle not in `E` stays fully solid, so an exempt actor cannot walk into a wall it was not already inside. The test is per rectangle, not total: on the `fixture_airlock` hull-line geometry a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles `[672, 696)` and `[696, 720)` keeps its TOTAL overlap at 128 cells while stepping east (one rectangle loses a column, the other gains one), so a total-area test would let it cross the hull line, while the per-rectangle test refuses that step because the east rectangle's own overlap grows; every move along the shared edge (both overlaps unchanged) and every move away (both shrink) stays admitted. `E` is computed afresh each tick from the current box (no stored flag; nothing persisted or hashed). Each exempt actor-tick increments `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (read 0 in a clean build) and, in debug, fires `diag.actor_in_footprint` (PIPE:727). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What "exempt actor-tick" counts (option (a), adopted).** `E` is computed from a `solid_in` query, and a stationary actor issues none (BDY-9), so the counter increments **once per actor-tick in which `E` was evaluated and found non-empty** (a tick on which the actor requested a non-zero step, so the query ran), **plus once at each detection event whose start-of-tick box test finds `E` non-empty** (placement, a transfer, a weld or cut for every actor on the touched bodies, `post_restore`): a detection event on an actor whose box intersects nothing adds nothing, so a clean weld, cut or restore leaves the counter at 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier wording read as an unconditional increment per event)*. An idle exempt actor therefore adds nothing on its idle ticks, and a trapped actor that stops pressing a key stops counting; the counter is a lower bound on exempt time, and its only contract is the QA gate "0 in a clean build" (CI, not a playtest alarm; Tuning Knobs). Stationary overlaps are made visible by the detection events, by the `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` probe below and by the debug tree-walk (PIPE:727), never by a per-tick query Body does not otherwise issue. A rectangle in `E` is fully solid for the actor again on the first tick whose start box no longer intersects it. **Nothing shoves**: `pos` is unchanged on every tick the actor does not step, and a push-out, shove or snap is struck (an unannounced displacement the player did not cause, P2; it contradicts PCI:650 "the body is never displaced" and LY-11). The rule is strictly tighter than PCI:650's literal "non-solid for that actor until the overlap clears" (PCI:650, PCI:1002); the additive wording row is routed to the Controller in 8.3. Detection happens at placement, at every transfer, at `post_restore` and on every stepping tick; a stationary actor issues no query, so a stationary overlap is caught at those events and by the debug tree-walk. **Exit containment (the second clause of the predicate; P1).** A sub-step that passes the overlap test is ALSO refused if its destination foot ORIGIN (the box top-centre, D.2) lies in no section of the actor's own body (D.10: `actor_section` would answer NONE for that origin). The test reads the sections of the actor's current `body_id` only, so a plate whose section has left the body (the B plate after a cut) is no longer floor for this purpose. The only exits from a hatch cap therefore lead back onto the body's own floor: no exempt sub-step can carry an actor out of the hull, and an exempt step never produces a NONE section. An actor whose START origin is already in no section (a defect, Edge Cases) may step only toward an origin that lies in a section. The reason is that a crew member standing outside the hull while their air, temperature and pressure still came from a room they had left would be a hidden stat contradicting what the world shows, which is the failure the Pillar 1 design test forbids. **What the predicate guarantees, and what it does not.** Any sub-step with a component away from a rectangle in `E` shrinks that rectangle's overlap, so a PARTIALLY overlapping box whose shrinking direction leads onto the body's own floor leaves in a bounded number of ticks and can never deepen. Three residuals are accepted and are defect-only paths: (i) a box wholly inside one rectangle (the common case, because `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 is less than the 24-px strip) has constant overlap until an edge crosses out, so it may exit on either side, including through a closed leaf, provided the destination origin lies in a section of the body (never out of the hull); (ii) a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles can only slide along their shared edge or back out, and if neither reaches open floor it stays exempt in place; (iii) **the cap trap:** an actor in a hatch cap whose only shrinking direction would put its origin outside the body cannot leave. The concrete case: after a restore of a save recorded in that pose against the Layout state holding plate A SOLID, an actor at `pos = (690, 282)` has the box `[682, 698) x [282, 290)` astride the east edge of the cap plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)` (plate B, `[696, 720)`, belongs to a section that is not part of this body); stepping west deepens the overlap (refused), stepping north or south keeps it (admitted by the overlap test) until the box meets the rectangles that are not in `E` and stay solid (D.11 gives the extent), and stepping east shrinks it and is admitted only while the destination origin is inside plate A: at `V_WALK` 2 the actor walks `pos.x` 690, 692, 694, 695 and the sub-step to 696 is refused (the origin would lie in no section of the body), so it rests inside the cap at `pos.x = 695` with `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` counting every tick on which it presses a key *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the counting rule above; the trap is a strip, not a point: box `[x - 8, x + 8)` straddles the plate's east edge for `pos.x` 689 to 695, where west deepens the overlap (120 to 128 at 689) and refused, so an east input converges to `pos.x = 695` from any start in the strip; from `pos.x` 680 to 688 the box lies wholly inside the plate, west keeps the overlap at 128 and is admitted, and the actor walks back onto the floor; in y the strip spans `pos.y` 240 to 328, the rows for which the box lies wholly inside the plate's rows `[240, 336)`, and at the margins `pos.y` 233 to 239 and 329 to 335 the neighbouring hull-wall rectangle joins `E` and the outcome depends on Layout's neighbour geometry, which the fixture does not fix — D.11 states the full admitted-move set)*. That is a stuck state, and it is not a safe one. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The exposure rule for a footprint-resident exempt actor, stated once (BDY-16, BDY-29, D.11 repeat it).** The first draft added that the trapped actor's "every air, heat and pressure reading ... is the reading of a section it is still in"; that sentence was false and is struck. Body guarantees only that `actor_section` answers a section of the actor's own body (the origin `(695, 282)` lies in plate A). Suit does not read the section: it reads Layout `room_at(section_id, actor_local_px)`, and Layout answers NONE for any point inside a wall footprint (LY-5, LY:905; a `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` hatch is a bare SOLID `HULL` plate with no room, LY-15), and Suit maps a NONE that is not `IN_POD` to EXPOSED (SE-3, SE:342; the Graph answers the exterior's atmosphere, LSG:206). **Rule (option (c), adopted): an exempt actor whose foot origin lies inside a footprint rectangle of its own body (the cap trap, and residual (i) while it stays inside) is EXPOSED: it takes the exterior's values (vacuum, anoxic, exterior temperature) on a pressurised ship until its origin leaves the footprint or the game restarts from the last autosave.** Options (a) and (b) were examined and rejected. (a) Layout owns the answer for a plate cell and it is NONE; Body cannot write "the adjoining room" over a designed neighbour, so that is an ASK to Layout (Open Question 31) that would supersede this paragraph if adopted. (b) "origin in a section AND `room_at != NONE`" cannot help here: the trapped actor's START origin is already inside the plate, so `room_at` already answers NONE; the one shrinking direction is refused by the same containment and every other direction is refused by the overlap rule, so (b) freezes the actor where it stands, still EXPOSED. **A door-leaf exemption is not exposed:** a closed leaf sits on the door's sill and `room_at` answers the door's `sill_room` there (LY-5), so only wall and hull-plate (cap) footprints read NONE. **How this meets Pillar 1:** the actor is exactly where its feet are, visibly inside the plate, and Suit's own instruments report the exterior band it is standing in (the bands and cues are Suit's); the world does not lie, but the guarantee is **visibility, not safety**, and no sentence of this GDD claims otherwise. Body offers no rescue (a push-out is struck); the primary guard is that the state is unreachable (Assembly's refusal, deferral and the P2 tell window, and BM4's apply-time refusal, BDY-24); recovery belongs to Assembly (a re-weld), to Save/Load (the death-restart) or to the content fix (Open Question 27). This is why **Assembly's refusal (player cut) and deferral plus the P2 tell window (system cut) are the primary guard, a named must-repeat** (BDY-24, 8.3), BM4's apply-time refusal stands behind them (BDY-24 (iii)), and this rule is only the residual net for a restore or a template defect; `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` in the debug overlay makes every such tick visible. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Trapped-actor probe and the restored-while-trapped case (diagnostic only, never a displacement; Body will never rescue).** At each detection event (placement, a transfer, `post_restore`, **and a weld or cut: at BM3 and BM4 the event covers EVERY actor on the bodies the mutator touched, moved or not, because the SOLID rectangle set changed under them — a box left in a SOLID rectangle by a template defect would otherwise first be seen at the next `post_restore`; a cut itself cannot create the D.11 cap trap, because BM4 refuses it first (BDY-24 (iii))**) Body runs, for every actor whose start box gives a non-empty `E`, a bounded read-only probe: for each of the four axis directions it repeats the admitted 1-px sub-step of this paragraph (overlap test plus exit containment) up to `TILE_PX` (48) times from the actor's pose, writing nothing, and asks whether the box reaches a pose that intersects no SOLID rectangle. If none of the four directions does, the actor is **TRAPPED**: `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` counts, the debug overlay shows it and the pure read `trapped_actors() -> actor_id[]` (ascending; recomputed on every read from current state and never cached, so a stale entry cannot suppress an autosave indefinitely; not persisted, not hashed) lists it. The probe costs at most 4 x 48 box-versus-`E` tests per flagged actor, at those events and on each `trapped_actors()` read (one `solid_in` query per actor to find `E`, at most `MAX_ACTORS` actors per read), never inside `body.integrate` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It exists for one case the restore path creates: **an autosave written while an actor was trapped restores the trap** (positions restore exactly, BDY-31), and the MVP death policy (restart from the last autosave) can then reload into it; the probe makes that visible on the restore, and Body's answer is none beyond that: the remedy is content and authoring validation (Assembly's refusal and deferral keep the state unreachable, BDY-24; Open Question 27) and Save/Load declining to write an autosave while `trapped_actors()` is non-empty, a MUST-REPEAT owned by Save/Load whose acceptance criterion lives in Save/Load's GDD (Open Question 33, 8.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was an optional ASK)*. The QA gate is `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` = 0 across every clean-build scenario (AC-BDY-29c). *Decides:* R7, CP-1, PCI:650, LY-11, P2. (auto: D.11 hatch fixture; bounded exit from a partial overlap)

---
## Tuning Knobs

Body is a nearly knobless system by design: it is a kinematic frame, and the things that make it feel right (the speeds, the cadence, the wall depth, the zoom) belong to its neighbours. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# review-receipts.sh — content-hash change detection for review skills.
#
# WHY HASHES, NOT GIT OR MTIME
# A review baseline must not depend on the user's commit habits. `git diff`
# needs a committed baseline; `git status` catches uncommitted edits but only
# relative to git's own view; file mtimes lie under backup restores and cloud
# sync (an old-mtime restore with new content silently escapes review — a
# false NEGATIVE, the dangerous direction). Hashing the bytes has neither
# problem: content changed <=> hash changed. The residual failure directions
# are false POSITIVES (re-review something unchanged — wasted tokens, never a
# missed review): a hash tool changing between stamp and check, a receipt
# file that was never written, or no hash tool at all (git, sha1sum, shasum),
# which makes everything read CHANGED and says so on stderr.
#
# ONE EXCEPTION, and it is deliberate. `check` stays silent on an absent
# LITERAL path that the receipt never stamped, because a caller may name an
# optional input on every run (/design-review does exactly this with the
# entity registry) and reporting it would block a legitimate skip. That
# silence is a false negative only if a caller passes a literal path it
# believes must exist — so callers name optional inputs and nothing else. A
# path the receipt DID stamp and that is now absent is not optional: the last
# review read it, and it reads GONE.
#
# THE RECEIPT IS ALSO A LIST. `check` compares every path the receipt stamps,
# not only the ones the caller names. The receipt records what the
# last review actually read; a caller's list can fall behind what its phases
# load, and a file it leaves out would otherwise never be compared -- which is
# how /architecture-review stood on an old report after an engine upgrade.

The only exits are request_restore or new_game. Layout's PLATE (A3) was already applied before BM4 refused, so there is no 'next autosave' of the faulted state to inspect. After a restore the state is the older save, which cannot contain the cut. The clause cannot be observed, and its rationale is muddled.
findings.fix: Rewrite the clause as: 'ends in FAULTED; the actor row is byte-identical to before the BM4 call (check-then-write); no autosave is written while FAULTED (spy count 0 on the Save/Load write path); the last autosave on disk is unchanged; and request_restore of it yields a state with no actor overlapping the hatch plates (`PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` = 0, `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` = 0).' findings.fix: Replace `AC-SL-149` with `AC-SL-151` at L139, L1042 and L1237. Re-grep Body for any AC-SL-14x.

findings.section: BDY-15, BDY-9, BDY-10, 8.3 Layout row, OQ 32, AC-BDY-117(ii), AC-BDY-125 - collision API vs Layout
findings.finding: CONFLICT with the owner (G1: Layout owns the API). Layout (L237) already defines the hot-path API as `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out: QueryBuffer)`. It fills a caller-owned buffer (keys PackedInt64Array, spans PackedInt32Array, flags PackedByteArray) and returns the record count, with no array returned. Body's text still says Layout's `solid_in` 'returns a fresh array each call'. It asks for a new `solid_in_into(body_id, aabb, out: PackedInt32Array)` returning rectangle indices. BDY-10 binds `collide` to that function. OQ 32 and the 8.3 'Layout (new additive asks)' row stay OPEN. AC-BDY-125 is marked CI-BLOCKED-ON a function that does not exist under that name or buffer type. Body has 0 hits for QueryBuffer. An implementer cannot call the function Body names. The sweep also needs rectangle spans, and Body's index-only buffer cannot supply them.
findings.fix: Conform Body to Layout's QueryBuffer. In BDY-9, BDY-10, BDY-15 and AC-BDY-117(ii), change the `collide` binding to `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out)`, with a QueryBuffer owned by `body.integrate` and sized once at boot. Delete the `solid_in_into` ASK. Close OQ 32 and the 8.3 row, keeping the 'stated cost for section_at' ask open (OQ 36). Unblock AC-BDY-125 by rewriting it against the QueryBuffer.

findings.section: BDY-5 / AC-BDY-1 / BDY-21 / BDY-31 / 3.6 - kernel CR-8 and R3 callable shapes (prior RECOMMENDED, still unlanded)
findings.finding: Block registration and callable shapes are stale against kernel CR-8 (L114) and R3. CR-8 makes `gameplay` (bool, mandatory) and `interpolated` mandatory. It also requires `snapshot(ctx)` (delivered via `ctx.put`, a deep copy), `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` (copies in, never retains `data`), `default_state(ctx)`, `read_view(ctx)` and `post_restore(ctx)`, each ending `return ctx.complete()`. Body has 0 hits for `default_state`, `read_view` and `ctx.put`. It never states `gameplay` or `interpolated`. BDY-31 still writes `snapshot()` returning plain data and `restore(data, stored_version)`. BDY-21 lists only `body.integrate`, snapshot, restore and post_restore as ctx callables. `seat_bindings()` (3.6) is a bare pure read, but the kernel's registered binding source is `binding_source(ctx)`, which delivers pairs through `ctx.put` and returns `ctx.complete()` (KRN-BIND-04 faults on a missing sentinel). AC-BDY-1 as written would pass a registration the kernel refuses at boot.
findings.fix: Add to BDY-5 and AC-BDY-1: `gameplay: true` (walking is a gameplay verb); `interpolated: false` (Body rolls pos_prev itself inside the hook, BDY-9); `default_state(ctx)` and `read_view(ctx)`. Restate BDY-31 as `snapshot(ctx)` and `restore(data, version, ctx)` with copy-in and an aliasing test (mutate the payload after restore and assert the block is unchanged). State that `seat_bindings()` remains the pure read and that a thin registered `binding_source(ctx)` calls it and delivers the pairs via `ctx.put`. Make AC-BDY-6 assert the pairs arrive through `ctx.put`.

findings.section: AC-BDY-141 and Edge Cases 'If a cut is applied anyway' - untestable clause
findings.finding: Quoted: 'ends in `FAULTED` with the actor unmoved and no overlap with the hatch plates in the saved bytes of the next autosave'. Edge Cases says 'The next autosave never holds the overlap (AC-BDY-141)'. The kernel (L174) states 'In FAULTED the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save'. The only exits are request_restore or new_game. Layout's PLATE (A3) was already applied before BM4 refused, so there is no 'next autosave' of the faulted state to inspect. After a restore the state is the older save, which cannot contain the cut. The clause cannot be observed, and its rationale is muddled.
findings.fix: Rewrite the clause as: 'ends in FAULTED; the actor row is byte-identical to before the BM4 call (check-then-write); no autosave is written while FAULTED (spy count 0 on the Save/Load write path); the last autosave on disk is unchanged; and request_restore of it yields a state with no actor overlapping the hatch plates (`PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` = 0, `BDY_TRAPPED_ACTOR` = 0).' Mirror the wording in the Edge Cases bullet.

findings.section: BM1 callers (L225 state table, L274 3.5, AC-BDY-107) - respawn (prior RECOMMENDED, still unfixed, G3)
findings.finding: 'respawn' is still listed as a BM1 caller in three places (state-table PLACED row L225, 3.5 BM1 row L274, AC-BDY-107 lint: 'BM1 is called only from `init_world` and respawn'). The user's ruling is that MVP death restarts from the last autosave, so no respawn function exists. The lint allow-list names a function that cannot exist and invites a phantom respawn path.
findings.fix: Delete 'respawn' in all three places. Rewrite AC-BDY-107's lint half as: 'BM1 is called only from `init_world` (the spawn tables of Transit and Authoring); a lint over the Body module finds no other BM1 caller'. Then Grep for 'respawn' and confirm zero hits (G3).

findings.section: D.13 / BDY-20 / AC-BDY-137 - actor_id range (prior RECOMMENDED, still unfixed)
findings.finding: D.13 states `id` is 'below 2^32' for the dirty key `(KIND << 32) | id`. `actor_id` is int64 and never reused (BDY-20, BDY-7). AC-BDY-137 sets an actor_id of 2^40 through a test hook. 2^40 shifted against `KIND << 32` collides with the KIND bits, so the key would be non-unique. BM1 has no guard against `next_actor_id` reaching 2^32, and restore has no reason code for it.
findings.fix: Add a rule and reason: BM1 returns `-BDY_PLACE_ID_EXHAUSTED` when `next_actor_id >= 2^32 - 1`, and restore rejects `next_actor_id` above that bound (`BDY_RESTORE_ACTOR_ID`). Change AC-BDY-137 to keep the 2^40 hook for the odometer column and use an actor_id below 2^32, plus a boundary AC for exhaustion.

findings.section: AC-BDY-117 (a)/(b) and D.12 - worst-case fixtures
findings.finding: D.12 states that W2 is NOT the most expensive exempt case: east is refused at the first sub-step, so n_sub = 1. It names W2b (n_sub = 6) and W2c (mixed) as the worst exempt and busy fixtures. AC-BDY-117 (a) and (b) still run only W1, W2 and W3, and (b) uses '4 * hook(W2)' as the catch-up worst frame. The (a)(i) bound 'at most K rectangle tests plus n_sub * |E| overlap evaluations with n_sub <= 6' is therefore never exercised at n_sub = 6, and the deterministic count gate cannot catch a regression in the costly path.
findings.fix: Change AC-BDY-117 (a) and (b) to 'W1, W2, W2b, W2c, W3' and use '4 * max(hook(W2b), hook(W2c))' for the catch-up frame. Add a count assertion for W2b: exactly 6 sub-steps and 6 section_at calls per exempt actor-tick.

findings.section: 8.3 rows, OQ 25/28/34/43/44 - stale OPEN statuses (known leftover pattern)
findings.finding: Several routed asks are marked OPEN although the sibling now conforms. (2) 8.3 'Modular Ship Assembly (design review, new)' (a) to (c): MSA L220 and L1696 say the C5 fallback in MSA-12 (3)(iii) is deleted, and A4 passes rects[] (L278). OQ 28 'Still OPEN: Assembly strikes the C5 fallback' is therefore stale. (3) OQ 34: Layout publishes `detach_preview` (LY-17, L277) and LY-28. (4) OQ 44 / 8.3 Pipeline row: PIPE L165 and L284 already treat a weld/detach BODY_TRANSFER with frame_delta_px as a rebase, so the confirmation is satisfied. (5) OQ 25 duplicates the already-recorded AC-BDY-90 result. Sibling leftovers also remain: MSA L984, L1248, L353 and L1887 still say the Pipeline's 'camera cut' hides the weld or fallback, which contradicts the REBASE (AC-BDY-118). Body's own text is correct.
findings.fix: Re-mark each Body row ANSWERED with the file and line evidence above. Close OQ 25, 28, 34, 43 and 44. Route the MSA L353/L984/L1248/L1887 wording to the Assembly writer ('camera cut' becomes 'camera REBASE; a cut only where bounds clamp'). Run a confirming grep after each edit (G3) and print patch counts.

findings.section: BDY-16 / OQ 33 / 8.3 Save/Load row / 3.6 trapped_actors - autosave-guard MUST-REPEAT
findings.finding: Body states, in three places, that Save/Load must decline or defer an autosave while `trapped_actors()` is non-empty, 'with its acceptance criterion in Save/Load's GDD'. save-load-and-versioned-format.md has no `trapped_actors` hit (its only 'trapped' hit is OQ-22, which does not mention Body). The must-repeat has not landed and the cited sibling AC does not exist. The consequence is bounded after this pass, since BM4 now refuses a cut and only an old save or a template defect can create the trap. But the death-restart loop can still reload a lethal EXPOSED state indefinitely if an autosave captured it.

findings.section: AC-BDY-68 (spike S1) - two pass states
findings.finding: Quoted: 'THEN P99 per-actor step cost is at most the cited 0.05 ms at K = 16 ... at most 0.2 ms ... at most 0.4 ms'. The same criterion then says 'a spike records, it does not gate on the unmeasured c_r' and 'pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK'. A QA tester cannot tell whether 0.05 ms is a threshold.
findings.fix: Rewrite the THEN as: 'THEN the P99 per-actor step cost, the 4-actor hook total and the 8-actor hook total are RECORDED for each fixture W1 to W5 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (release export, R12). The cited 0.05 / 0.2 / 0.4 ms are the comparison values, not pass lines. The recorded numbers become the AC-BDY-117(b) baseline. Pass = the record file exists with all fixtures and both machines.'

findings.section: AC-BDY-69 - threshold wording
findings.finding: The same criterion says 'no frame of the 600-frame window may exceed that machine's P99 frame-time ceiling' while R12's headroom rule is 'P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling'. A maximum is stricter than a P99, so the two rules disagree. The 8 ms figure is also justified as 'half a 16.7 ms frame at 60 Hz', which is inapplicable to RM-DECK (33.3 ms).
findings.fix: State one rule: P99 of the weld-frame projector work <= 8 ms on both machines, and P99 of the 600-frame window <= 90 % of the ceiling (14.9 ms and 30.0 ms). Drop the 60 Hz justification, or state it for RM-DESKTOP only.

findings.section: AC-BDY-110 / AC-BDY-70 - golden file
findings.finding: Both ACs depend on a golden file 'frozen at the kernel spike', which does not exist yet. The 518 bytes are fully derivable by hand from the kernel's D.12 worked examples. The AC can only pass once a spike that is not Body's has run.
findings.fix: Add the hand-derived header and key section as an inline fixture (tag 08, count 5, the five encoded keys in sorted order). The committed golden file then only has to confirm the values section. This is not blocking; spike-gated criteria are intentional.

findings.section: Dependencies opening paragraph (L770) and OQ preamble
findings.finding: The 2026-10-26 status paragraph still says Modular Ship Assembly, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Boarding & Salvage, Sanity, Perception Filter and Debug Overlay have 'no file'. It is superseded only by an inline Amended note. All Dependencies systems have a GDD on disk (verified by Glob). Nothing is missing, and no R9 undesigned item applies to this GDD. findings.section: OQ 47 / 8.3 Kernel row - restore-time reads
findings.finding: The kernel has not confirmed that a block's `restore()` may call the pure reads of a block it lists in `restore_after`. `BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY` (BDY-31, AC-BDY-56) depends on it. restore_after Layout guarantees Layout is restored first, so the dependency is sound. findings.fix: Ask the kernel writer to add one sentence to CR-8 or CR-15 permitting pure reads of restore_after blocks inside restore(). If declined, move the live-body check to post_restore and update AC-BDY-56/120.

findings.section: AC-BDY-141 cross-reference

findings.fix: Add 'twin: AC-MSA-151' to AC-BDY-141, and list AC-BDY-141 among the neighbour-owned (Assembly) criteria.
